Sounds like you need to figure out what you want to do. I recommend forgetting the career counselor catalog of job titles and think about activities you like, such as: do you need to be indoors or outdoors, do you like to interact with people or do they wear you out, do you like to think, write and sit at a desk, or do you need to be active and work with your hands? What are the predominant fields in your area (gross opportunities) or are you willing to move?

Having a family business is a great way to expose yourself to the different areas so dive in and try things in operations, management, finance, sales, or R&D. Do you like to make the product or delegate and manage resources and people? Do you like the detail work of the general ledger and AR/AP or strategic planning and driving new ideas and new products? If you hate customers stay in production or management, but if you have that "way" with people you could drive revenue with sales and growth.

Try some new things out and see what you like. The job title doesn't matter. Seek the activities you like and the titles will flow naturally from there.

Also, reaffirming previous comments on "Do you really want to be a lawyer?" The school doesn't matter unless you go to ivy and for everyone else it's no magic career saver. Only 50% of law school grads actually end up practicing and even then the pay isn't that great. It isn't what you see on television with the wood paneled office, swanky secretary, and the B'mer. That just doesn't happen for the working class lawyer. It's just a job, one which is being abandoned by many after a few years of practice, so really give it some thought before committing.
